Pooled result

MD -53.97 (-58.3 to -49.64), 95% interval

Multiple trial-declared outcomes: Percent Change in LDL-C From Baseline To Day 510 | Percentage Change in LDL-C From Baseline to Day 510. random-effects, estimator REML, k = 3.

τ² 10.6 · I² 74.1% · Q 7.143 on 2 df

Favours: the intervention (lower is better)

Q = 7.1426 on 2 df, I-squared 74.1 per cent, tau-squared 10.60 under REML.

The pool STANDS, and every STEP of it was checked rather than assumed. The estimand is the same in all three registrations. ORION-9 registers 'Percent Change in LDL-C From Baseline To Day 510'; ORION-10 and ORION-11 register 'Percentage Change in LDL-C From Baseline to Day 510'. Same quantity, same anchor, same day, all three analysed by ancova and reported by the registry as a 'Mean Difference (Final Values)'. The only difference between the three strings is 'Percent' against 'Percentage' -- orthography, which is precisely the trap that has manufactured false disagreements in this repository before, and it is not one here. All three per-trial values are the registry's own, digit for digit: orion-9 -49.52 (-55.04 to -43.99), ORION-10 -57.64 (-60.86 to -54.43), ORION-11 -53.50 (-56.66 to -50.35). All three arm pairs sum to their registration's recorded enrolment exactly: 242+240=482, 781+780=1561, 810+807=1617. Arm labels and roles are correct on all three. And the pooled value reproduces: REML inverse-variance random effects on the three mean differences gives -54.0014 (-58.1652 to -49.8377), which is what the object holds and what the index card publishes, to four decimal places. The card, the object and the independent recomputation all agree. [restated 2026-08-20. This sentence was written while the pool was fitted with DerSimonian-Laird inverse-variance on extracted effect estimates. It is now REML, under DECISIONS-COCHRANE-2026-08-18.md section 1, on Cochrane Handbook 6.5 section 10.10.4.4: "Decision: REML, everywhere." The estimate moved from -54.00144508917459 (-58.16516691761607 to -49.83772326073311) to -53.97 (-58.3 to -49.64) and tau-squared from 9.524722803298308 to 10.595364. The original wording is beside this under poolable_reason_superseded_2026_08_20 -- a sentence that recorded a decision is restated, never deleted.]

Why this pool stands. The pool STANDS, and every STEP of it was checked rather than assumed. The estimand is the same in all three registrations. ORION-9 registers 'Percent Change in LDL-C From Baseline To Day 510'; ORION-10 and ORION-11 register 'Percentage Change in LDL-C From Baseline to Day 510'. Same quantity, same anchor, same day, all three analysed by ancova and reported by the registry as a 'Mean Difference (Final Values)'. The only difference between the three strings is 'Percent' against 'Percentage' -- orthography, which is precisely the trap that has manufactured false disagreements in this repository before, and it is not one here. All three per-trial values are the registry's own, digit for digit: orion-9 -49.52 (-55.04 to -43.99), ORION-10 -57.64 (-60.86 to -54.43), ORION-11 -53.50 (-56.66 to -50.35). All three arm pairs sum to their registration's recorded enrolment exactly: 242+240=482, 781+780=1561, 810+807=1617. Arm labels and roles are correct on all three. And the pooled value reproduces: REML inverse-variance random effects on the three mean differences gives -54.0014 (-58.1652 to -49.8377), which is what the object holds and what the index card publishes, to four decimal places. The card, the object and the independent recomputation all agree. [restated 2026-08-20: this pool is now fitted with REML under DECISIONS-COCHRANE-2026-08-18.md section 1, on Cochrane Handbook 6.5 section 10.10.4.4: "Decision: REML, everywhere.", so the caveat that its estimator was not this project's standard for its k no longer applies. The sentence is kept, restated, rather than deleted, because a reader who saw the old one should be able to see what became of it.]

What a reader should know anyway, none of which overturns the estimate. (1) the estimator is not this project's own standard for this k. REML underestimates between-study variance when k is small, and the house rule is REML or REML below k=10. This pool is k=3. It was recomputed under both: REML gives -53.95 (-58.40 to -49.51) with tau-squared 11.36, REML gives -53.97 (-58.30 to -49.64) with tau-squared 10.60, against DL's -54.00 (-58.17 to -49.84) with tau-squared 9.52. The point estimate moves by five hundredths of a percentage point on a scale of fifty-four. The choice of estimator does not change this answer, and the published value is retained rather than re-rounded, because moving a correct published number by 0.05 would break every reader's record for no gain. Whether the corpus headline should move to REML everywhere is a display-change policy question, not a finding about this topic. (2) heterogeneity is HIGH and k is small: Q = 7.14 on 2 degrees of freedom, I-squared 72 per cent. A Hartung-Knapp interval, which is the honest one at this k, is -63.71 to -44.30 -- much wider than the Wald interval on the card. The direction and the magnitude are not in doubt; the precision on the card is optimistic. (3) the three populations are not the same: orion-9 enrolled heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia, ORION-10 atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, ORION-11 ascvd or risk-equivalents. That is a real clinical difference and the most likely source of the heterogeneity above. It is not an estimand difference -- all three measured the same thing on different people -- but it is why a single number should not be read as applying uniformly to all three groups. (4) ldl-c percent change is a surrogate. This review pools a laboratory value, not an event. Nothing here estimates an effect on death, myocardial infarction or stroke, and no such claim should be read into it. (5) one stored interval bound is reconstructed rather than read: orion-11's upper limit is held as -50.34 where the registry prints -50.35, a rounding artefact of recomputing the interval from a point estimate and a standard error. One hundredth of a percentage point, recorded because a reader comparing the two should not have to wonder whether it means something. [restated 2026-08-20: this pool is now fitted with REML under DECISIONS-COCHRANE-2026-08-18.md section 1, on Cochrane Handbook 6.5 section 10.10.4.4: "Decision: REML, everywhere.", so the caveat that its estimator was not this project's standard for its k no longer applies. The sentence is kept, restated, rather than deleted, because a reader who saw the old one should be able to see what became of it.]

All three trials register two co-primary outcomes: percentage change in LDL-C from baseline to DAY 510, and the TIME-ADJUSTED percentage change after day 90 up to day 540. This pool uses the first. The selection is recorded nowhere. The two answer different questions about a drug given twice a year -- a single timepoint against an average across the dosing interval -- and a review that selects among registered options without recording the selection has made an analytic decision that cannot be audited from its own output. The estimate is not changed here: choosing the other co-primary is a content decision.

Read this beside the estimate. All three trials registered two co-primary outcomes: the percent change in LDL-C at Day 510, which this pool uses, and the TIME-ADJUSTED percent change from baseline after day 90 and up to day 540, which it does not. Pooling the other one by the same method gives -49.30 (-54.52 to -44.07) against this pool's -53.97 (-58.30 to -49.64). The choice of co-primary moves the headline by 4.7 percentage points, and until now this object said nowhere that a second one existed. Both are stored; neither is withdrawn; which one answers a given question is not a choice this page can make for a reader.

A cross-lane check reported this pool's point as wrong for its own estimand -- -53.97 against roughly -50.6 -- and its heterogeneity as largely an extraction artefact. Both were checked against the posted results on 2026-08-21 and neither holds. Every per-trial value here reproduces its registration's own Day-510 mean-difference analysis exactly: -49.52 (-55.04 to -43.99), -57.64 (-60.86 to -54.43), -53.50 (-56.66 to -50.35). The ~-50.6 is the other co-primary, recorded above. The reported defect was a comparison against a different estimand, and it is written here rather than dropped because a check that was run and did not hold is evidence too.

I-squared is 74.1% with tau-squared 10.60 on this pool. On the other co-primary it is 87.9% with tau-squared 18.89. The spread is not an artefact of how these numbers were read; it is larger on the estimand that was said to be cleaner.

Leave-one-out sensitivity

Two decisions. First, whether the pooled reduction depends on any single trial. Second, whether it depends on the between-study variance estimator and interval method -- which at k=3, with the house rule against REML below k=10, is not a formality but the reason this table exists. No single trial carries this result. Omitting each in turn gives -55.56 (-59.62 to -51.50), -52.18 (-55.85 to -48.51) and -53.90 (-61.84 to -45.97). All three exclude no effect and the pooled point moves by at most 1.8 percentage points on a scale of 54.

Cochrane Handbook version 6.5.1, section 10.10.4.4: methods other than DerSimonian and Laird estimate the between-study variance better, and restricted maximum likelihood is the RevMan default. Section 10.14 governs the leave-one-out half. Cited to 10.10.4.4 rather than 10.10.4.5 because 10.10.4.5 is about interpretation with few studies and the method it compares is the confidence interval, not the variance estimator -- a miscitation this repository has already made once and corrected.

Does the answer depend on the pooling method?

Three between-study-variance estimators, each with Wald and Hartung-Knapp intervals. This pool is published under REML at k=3, and this project's own rule is REML or REML below k=10, so the first question a reader should be able to answer is whether that choice made the answer. [restated 2026-08-20. This sentence was written while the pool was fitted with DerSimonian-Laird inverse-variance on extracted effect estimates. It did not. The point estimate spans -53.95 to -53.97 across all six combinations -- a range of five hundredths on a scale of fifty-four -- and every one of the six intervals excludes no effect, the widest by more than forty percentage points. The interval, not the point, is what the method changes: Wald gives about -58 to -50 and Hartung-Knapp about -64 to -44, roughly twice the width. At k=3 with I-squared of 72 per cent, hartung-knapp is the honest one, and the precision shown on the index card is optimistic even though its direction and magnitude are not in doubt. [restated 2026-08-20: this sentence carried the pooled estimate as it stood under DerSimonian-Laird inverse-variance on extracted effect estimates. The pool was refitted with REML under DECISIONS-COCHRANE-2026-08-18.md section 1, on Cochrane Handbook 6.5 section 10.10.4.4: "Decision: REML, everywhere." and the estimate is now -53.97 (-58.3 to -49.64); the numbers in this sentence are updated and the original is beside it under verdict_superseded_2026_08_20. Found by a number guard, not by the estimator guard -- a sentence can carry a superseded estimate without naming an estimator, and two such sentences survived this whole pass in the published comparison before one was noticed on the rendered page.

The published REML value is retained as the headline. Components as the registry states thempercent change in LDL-C from baseline to DAY 510. One continuous quantity, one anchor, one time point. No composite and no components.

Estimator kept supersededThe published DerSimonian-Laird value is retained as the headline. It reproduces exactly, and moving a correct published number by five hundredths of a percentage point would break every reader's record for no gain. Whether the corpus headline should move to REML everywhere is a display-change policy question for the whole corpus, not a finding about this topic, and it is parked as such.
Decision under test supersededTwo decisions. First, whether the pooled reduction depends on any single trial. Second, whether it depends on the between-study variance estimator and interval method -- which at k=3, with the house rule against DerSimonian-Laird below k=10, is not a formality but the reason this table exists.
CaveatsWhat a reader should know anyway, none of which overturns the estimate. (1) the estimator is not this project's own standard for this k. REML underestimates between-study variance when k is small, and the house rule is REML or REML below k=10. This pool is k=3. It was recomputed under both: REML gives -53.95 (-58.40 to -49.51) with tau-squared 11.36, REML gives -53.97 (-58.30 to -49.64) with tau-squared 10.60, against DL's -54.00 (-58.17 to -49.84) with tau-squared 9.52. The point estimate moves by five hundredths of a percentage point on a scale of fifty-four. The choice of estimator does not change this answer, and the published value is retained rather than re-rounded, because moving a correct published number by 0.05 would break every reader's record for no gain. Whether the corpus headline should move to REML everywhere is a display-change policy question, not a finding about this topic. (2) heterogeneity is HIGH and k is small: Q = 7.14 on 2 degrees of freedom, I-squared 72 per cent. A Hartung-Knapp interval, which is the honest one at this k, is -63.71 to -44.30 -- much wider than the Wald interval on the card. The direction and the magnitude are not in doubt; the precision on the card is optimistic. (3) the three populations are not the same: orion-9 enrolled heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia, ORION-10 atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, ORION-11 ascvd or risk-equivalents. That is a real clinical difference and the most likely source of the heterogeneity above. It is not an estimand difference -- all three measured the same thing on different people -- but it is why a single number should not be read as applying uniformly to all three groups. (4) ldl-c percent change is a surrogate. This review pools a laboratory value, not an event. Nothing here estimates an effect on death, myocardial infarction or stroke, and no such claim should be read into it. (5) one stored interval bound is reconstructed rather than read: orion-11's upper limit is held as -50.34 where the registry prints -50.35, a rounding artefact of recomputing the interval from a point estimate and a standard error. One hundredth of a percentage point, recorded because a reader comparing the two should not have to wonder whether it means something. Stands because supersededThe pool STANDS, and every STEP of it was checked rather than assumed. The estimand is the same in all three registrations. ORION-9 registers 'Percent Change in LDL-C From Baseline To Day 510'; ORION-10 and ORION-11 register 'Percentage Change in LDL-C From Baseline to Day 510'. Same quantity, same anchor, same day, all three analysed by ancova and reported by the registry as a 'Mean Difference (Final Values)'. The only difference between the three strings is 'Percent' against 'Percentage' -- orthography, which is precisely the trap that has manufactured false disagreements in this repository before, and it is not one here. All three per-trial values are the registry's own, digit for digit: orion-9 -49.52 (-55.04 to -43.99), ORION-10 -57.64 (-60.86 to -54.43), ORION-11 -53.50 (-56.66 to -50.35). All three arm pairs sum to their registration's recorded enrolment exactly: 242+240=482, 781+780=1561, 810+807=1617. Arm labels and roles are correct on all three. And the pooled value reproduces: DerSimonian-Laird inverse-variance random effects on the three mean differences gives -54.0014 (-58.1652 to -49.8377), which is what the object holds and what the index card publishes, to four decimal places. The card, the object and the independent recomputation all agree.

A two co primaries were registered and one is pooledAll three trials register two co-primary outcomes: percentage change in LDL-C from baseline to DAY 510, and the TIME-ADJUSTED percentage change after day 90 up to day 540. This pool uses the first. The selection is recorded nowhere. The two answer different questions about a drug given twice a year -- a single timepoint against an average across the dosing interval -- and a review that selects among registered options without recording the selection has made an analytic decision that cannot be audited from its own output. The estimate is not changed here: choosing the other co-primary is a content decision.
A each trial registered two co primaries and this pools oneRead this beside the estimate. All three trials registered two co-primary outcomes: the percent change in LDL-C at Day 510, which this pool uses, and the TIME-ADJUSTED percent change from baseline after day 90 and up to day 540, which it does not. Pooling the other one by the same method gives -49.30 (-54.52 to -44.07) against this pool's -53.97 (-58.30 to -49.64). The choice of co-primary moves the headline by 4.7 percentage points, and until now this object said nowhere that a second one existed. Both are stored; neither is withdrawn; which one answers a given question is not a choice this page can make for a reader.
B the extraction was checked against the registrations and is exactA cross-lane check reported this pool's point as wrong for its own estimand -- -53.97 against roughly -50.6 -- and its heterogeneity as largely an extraction artefact. Both were checked against the posted results on 2026-08-21 and neither holds. Every per-trial value here reproduces its registration's own Day-510 mean-difference analysis exactly: -49.52 (-55.04 to -43.99), -57.64 (-60.86 to -54.43), -53.50 (-56.66 to -50.35). The ~-50.6 is the other co-primary, recorded above. The reported defect was a comparison against a different estimand, and it is written here rather than dropped because a check that was run and did not hold is evidence too.
C the heterogeneity is real and the alternative is worseI-squared is 74.1% with tau-squared 10.60 on this pool. On the other co-primary it is 87.9% with tau-squared 18.89. The spread is not an artefact of how these numbers were read; it is larger on the estimand that was said to be cleaner.
Scopeinclisiran 284 mg, reported separately from the PCSK9 antibodies
Scopenetwork meta-analysis placing inclisiran against evolocumab, alirocumab, bempedoic acid and ezetimibe
What this denominator does not coverThe 51 records the screen retrieved and did not read. The check count is honest about the checks; the screen is separately honest about its own size in the appraisal file, and neither number should be read as the other.
What is not establishedThe concealment mechanism is not on the registry, and the published reports were not read. LOW is scored on the recorded allocation, not on a mechanism nobody here has seen.
Why this is not an adjudicated disputeA blind second assessor from a different model family disagreed with this domain on 89% of judgements across 22 topics. That would ordinarily be a dispute to adjudicate. It is not one: the tool's own text names this exact evidential situation -- a bare statement that a study was randomised -- and prescribes the answer. The second assessor is not being deferred to; the guidance is being applied.
What the registry gives and does notA ClinicalTrials.gov design module records `allocation: Randomized`. It carries no sequence-generation method and no allocation-concealment mechanism. The original judgement's own note said so before scoring LOW.
How this maps to the tool s algorithmThe tool maps 'No information' on 1.1 and 1.2 with no baseline concern to a domain judgement of some concerns. This project writes NO_INFORMATION on the domain when it could not be judged from the sources read, and caps the overall at SOME_CONCERNS. Same place, and it keeps 'we could not judge this' distinguishable from 'we judged it and had concerns'.
What does not changeNo overall rating and no GRADE CERTAINTY moves. All 51 judgements were already capped at SOME_CONCERNS or HIGH by another NO_INFORMATION domain.
Why this profile differs from its siblingsAgainst empagliflozin: that result is an adjudicated time-to-event composite, so D3 is LOW because censoring absorbs withdrawal and D4 is LOW because a blinded committee adjudicates. Against icosapent: the same fixed-timepoint laboratory shape, but at DAY 510 rather than week 12, so the D3 threat is materially larger for the same reasoning. D5 is SOME_CONCERNS here for a different reason than icosapent's -- there a dose arm was selected from three, here a co-primary was selected from two.
And it bounds a finding of oursClass 94 records assessor 2 saying NO_INFORMATION on D1/D2/D3 `100 of 100`. Measured across all 23 topics now stored that is 239 of 243, and all four exceptions are D1=SOME_CONCERNS on `agyw-hiv-prep-review` and `cab-prep-hiv-review` -- two of the three topics asked under the earlier prompt build, the one whose reply ids are bare NCTs. Under that build it is 4 of 6; under the later build 0 of 75. The 100% was measured on the later build's topics. The two-defaults mechanism stands; its universality does not, and what varies with it is the prompt.
The rate is still conditional on the same allow listBoth numbers are conditional on the fact list in THE_ALLOW_LIST_THE_RATE_IS_CONDITIONAL_ON above. Neither is a rate of agreement between assessors in general.
Scope correctedThis topic is named `inclisiran-lipid-kidney` and it analyses no kidney outcome. Every result on this object is LDL-C percent change. No renal endpoint -- eGFR, albuminuria, kidney failure, dialysis -- is extracted, pooled, assessed for risk of bias or rated for certainty anywhere here. The slug is retained because it is the key a reader's URL resolves through and changing it would break a page a reader may already hold; the scope is corrected here instead. What this review covers: the effect of inclisiran on LDL-C. What it does not cover, despite its name: anything renal.
Which risk of bias domains drove the ratingWhere a result is rated worse than LOW overall, the domain carrying that judgement is: D5 on 3 result(s). The overall rating is the worst domain, so these are the domains that determine it.

Comparison with published syntheses

Three trials, one drug, one endpoint, and every per-trial value posted by the registry -- so the trial-by-trial half of this comparison is complete in a way it cannot be where trials post no results. The error found is ours and it is in the table below with the same weight as anything found in the literature.

9 checks were applied and 6 came back clean, 1 found an error, 1 found something absent and 1 could not be settled at the layer available. The denominator is stated because a list of only the failures is not a finding, it is a selection.

Confirmations are listed in the same table, in the same detail, as errors. The one error found is ours -- an unrecorded selection between two registered co-primary endpoints -- and the published literature is implicated in none of the rows. That is the same result every cardiology topic reconciled in this corpus has produced, and a comparison with room only for their errors could not have found it out.

The syntheses reconciled against

Table 14. The syntheses reconciled against
32892993Khan SA, Naz A, Qamar Masood M, Shah R. Meta-Analysis of Inclisiran for the Treatment of Hypercholesterolemia. Am J Cardiol 2020;134:69-73. doi 10.1016/j.amjcard.2020.08.018
By arithmetic and timing it pools this review's own three trials -- its n of 3,660 is exactly their summed arm counts, and it was published five months after they reported. Its -51% (48 to 53) against this review's -53.97% is therefore a difference in extraction OR endpoint rather than in trial set, which is what makes it the most informative row here.
38055686Imran TF, et al. PCSK9 inhibitors and small interfering RNA therapy for cardiovascular risk reduction: a systematic review and meta-analysis. PLoS One 2023;18(12):e0295359. doi 10.1371/journal.pone.0295359
Four inclisiran studies rather than three, across a broader population. Lands within one percentage point of this review.
40565909Alaiz AR, et al. Inclisiran: Efficacy in Real World -- Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. J Clin Med 2025;14(12):4163. doi 10.3390/jcm14124163
A different design, not a different trial set: single-arm observational change against a randomised placebo-corrected difference. It cannot confirm or contradict this review and is listed so the reader knows the question was asked.
35262430Burnett H, et al. Comparative efficacy of non-statin lipid-lowering therapies in patients with hypercholesterolemia at increased cardiovascular risk: a network meta-analysis. Curr Med Res Opin 2022;38(5):777-784. doi 10.1080/03007995.2022.2049164
A different question -- relative efficacy between active agents, not the size of the effect against placebo. Its own reported heterogeneity is 'roughly equivalent to variation of 5-10% change in LDL-C', which is larger than the gap between this review and Khan 2020.

Where the numbers differ, and why

Table 15. Where the numbers differ, and why
This reviewMean difference -53.97% (-58.30 to -49.64) in LDL-C percent change from baseline to day 510, k=3, random effects, REML.
The published synthesis-51% (48 to 53) over what is by arithmetic the same three trials; -54.83% (-59.04 to -50.62) over four; -42.77% (37.42 to 48.12) over seven real-world cohorts; and a network analysis reporting relative rather than absolute effect.
Why they differNot by trial set, which is the unusual and useful thing about this comparison. The closest synthesis pools the same three trials and differs by about three percentage points, so the difference is in extraction or in which registered co-primary was taken -- day 510, or time-adjusted day 90 to 540. This review's own selection between those two is consistent across all three trials and was never recorded, which is the error listed above. The broader syntheses agree with this review closely; the real-world pooling does not, and its own authors attribute that to baseline LDL-C and adherence rather than to either estimate being wrong.

How they were identified: PubMed E-utilities; query, counts and a per-record decision in ssot/inclisiran-lipid-kidney-auto-full-review/appraisal/PUBLISHED_SYNTHESIS_SCREEN.json. 61 records matched, 30 retrieved, 10 appraised. The remaining 51 were not read and that is stated in the screen file rather than left to be inferred from the number.

Title and review question

Inclisiran for elevated low-density lipoprotein cholesterol in HeFH, ascvd or ASCVD-risk equivalents1

This topic is named `inclisiran-lipid-kidney` and it analyses no kidney outcome. Every result on this object is LDL-C percent change. No renal endpoint -- eGFR, albuminuria, kidney failure, dialysis -- is extracted, pooled, assessed for risk of bias or rated for certainty anywhere here. The slug is retained because it is the key a reader's URL resolves through and changing it would break a page a reader may already hold; the scope is corrected here instead. What this review covers: the effect of inclisiran on LDL-C. What it does not cover, despite its name: anything renal.2

In Inclisiran for elevated low-density lipoprotein cholesterol in HeFH, ascvd or ASCVD-risk equivalents, what do the contributing trials show?3

Abstract

Question. In Inclisiran for elevated low-density lipoprotein cholesterol in HeFH, ascvd or ASCVD-risk equivalents, what do the contributing trials show?1

Methods. estimates were pooled under a random-effects with the REML estimator; risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials); and certainty was rated with GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons.2

Results. Multiple trial-declared outcomes: Percent Change in LDL-C From Baseline To Day 510 | Percentage Change in LDL-C From Baseline to Day 510: mean difference -54 (-58.3 to -49.6) across 3 trials; 1 of these pooled outcome(s) carries a stated qualification -- a referral or a recorded finding -- given in full in Results and not reproduced here; the trials agreed loosely (I-squared 74.1%); and certainty of the evidence was very low.3

Introduction

1Background. This review asks: In Inclisiran for elevated low-density lipoprotein cholesterol in HeFH, ascvd or ASCVD-risk equivalents, what do the contributing trials show? It pools 3 randomised trials. The outcome pooled is Multiple trial-declared outcomes: Percent Change in LDL-C From Baseline To Day 510 | Percentage Change in LDL-C From Baseline to Day 510.

[Draft] The evidence identified on this question is 3 randomised trials (NCT03397121, NCT03399370, NCT03400800), pooled here at -53.97 (95% CI -58.3 to -49.64) for primary. Certainty in that estimate is rated VERY_LOW. Which of those unresolved points makes the question worth asking now is the author's judgement.2

[Draft] A search for published syntheses matched an unrecorded number of record(s); an unrecorded number were read and an unrecorded number appraised against this review. The appraised synthesis is an untitled record. Whether those differences warrant a new synthesis rather than citing the existing one is the author's judgement.3

Methods — synthesis

For multiple trial-declared outcomes: Percent Change in LDL-C From Baseline To Day 510 | Percentage Change in LDL-C From Baseline to Day 510, a random-effects model was fitted with the REML estimator.1

Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials) (), following . 3 result-level assessments were made.2

A ceiling applies to every risk-of-bias judgement in this review; it is stated with the assessment itself rather than summarised here.3

Certainty of evidence was rated with GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons., following . 0 pooled outcome(s) were rated. No domain is rated UP. Rating up for a large effect or a dose-response gradient applies to observational evidence that has not already been rated down, and neither condition holds here. 1 outcome(s) were not rated because their pool is declined or withdrawn: there is no effect estimate to rate the certainty of, and rating one would be certainty about a number this review refused to publish.4

Results

The pooled mean difference for multiple trial-declared outcomes: Percent Change in LDL-C From Baseline To Day 510 | Percentage Change in LDL-C From Baseline to Day 510 was -54 (-58.3 to -49.6) across 3 trials.1

Noted on this pool. All three trials register two co-primary outcomes: percentage change in LDL-C from baseline to DAY 510, and the TIME-ADJUSTED percentage change after day 90 up to day 540. This pool uses the first. The selection is recorded nowhere. The two answer different questions about a drug given twice a year -- a single timepoint against an average across the dosing interval -- and a review that selects among registered options without recording the selection has made an analytic decision that cannot be audited from its own output. The estimate is not changed here: choosing the other co-primary is a content decision. Read this beside the estimate. All three trials registered two co-primary outcomes: the percent change in LDL-C at Day 510, which this pool uses, and the TIME-ADJUSTED percent change from baseline after day 90 and up to day 540, which it does not. Pooling the other one by the same method gives -49.30 (-54.52 to -44.07) against this pool's -53.97 (-58.30 to -49.64). The choice of co-primary moves the headline by 4.7 percentage points, and until now this object said nowhere that a second one existed. Both are stored; neither is withdrawn; which one answers a given question is not a choice this page can make for a reader. A cross-lane check reported this pool's point as wrong for its own estimand -- -53.97 against roughly -50.6 -- and its heterogeneity as largely an extraction artefact. Both were checked against the posted results on 2026-08-21 and neither holds. Every per-trial value here reproduces its registration's own Day-510 mean-difference analysis exactly: -49.52 (-55.04 to -43.99), -57.64 (-60.86 to -54.43), -53.50 (-56.66 to -50.35). The ~-50.6 is the other co-primary, recorded above. The reported defect was a comparison against a different estimand, and it is written here rather than dropped because a check that was run and did not hold is evidence too. I-squared is 74.1% with tau-squared 10.60 on this pool. On the other co-primary it is 87.9% with tau-squared 18.89. The spread is not an artefact of how these numbers were read; it is larger on the estimand that was said to be cleaner.2

The trials' results were loosely consistent with one another: I-squared, the share of the variation between them that is more than chance alone would produce, was 74.1%; the estimated variance of the true effects between trials (tau-squared) was 10.6, the heterogeneity test statistic Q was 7.14, on degrees of freedom 2. Q = 7.1426 on 2 df, I-squared 74.1 per cent, tau-squared 10.60 under REML.3

The grounds for pooling are recorded as: The pool stands, and every STEP of it was checked rather than assumed. The estimand is the same in all three registrations. ORION-9 registers 'Percent Change in LDL-C From Baseline To Day 510'; ORION-10 and ORION-11 register 'Percentage Change in LDL-C From Baseline to Day 510'. Same quantity, same anchor, same day, all three analysed by ancova and reported by the registry as a 'Mean Difference (Final Values)'. The only difference between the three strings is 'Percent' against 'Percentage' -- orthography, which is precisely the trap that has manufactured false disagreements in this repository before, and it is not one here. All three per-trial values are the registry's own, digit for digit: orion-9 -49.52 (-55.04 to -43.99), ORION-10 -57.64 (-60.86 to -54.43), ORION-11 -53.50 (-56.66 to -50.35). All three arm pairs sum to their registration's recorded enrolment exactly: 242+240=482, 781+780=1561, 810+807=1617. Arm labels and roles are correct on all three. And the pooled value reproduces: REML inverse-variance random effects on the three mean differences gives -54.0014 (-58.1652 to -49.8377), which is what the object holds and what the index card publishes, to four decimal places. The card, the object and the independent recomputation all agree. [restated 2026-08-20. This sentence was written while the pool was fitted with DerSimonian-Laird inverse-variance on extracted effect estimates. It is now REML, under DECISIONS-COCHRANE-2026-08-18.md section 1, on Cochrane Handbook 6.5 section 10.10.4.4: "Decision: REML, everywhere." The estimate moved from -54.00144508917459 (-58.16516691761607 to -49.83772326073311) to -53.97 (-58.3 to -49.64) and tau-squared from 9.524722803298308 to 10.595364. The original wording is beside this under poolable_reason_superseded_2026_08_20 -- a sentence that recorded a decision is restated, never deleted.] Where a later pool on this page rests on the same grounds, they are not restated.4

The full model output for every pooled outcome -- the call, the estimator, the heterogeneity statistics and the back-transformed interval -- is reproduced verbatim as Extended data at the end of this article, so every number above can be checked against the software that produced it.5

Risk of bias in the included results

Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials). The unit of assessment is a result1

A domain that cannot be judged from the sources read is NO_INFORMATION, never LOW. Low-by-default asserts a fact; high-by-default invents a defect. Overall is capped at SOME_CONCERNS wherever a domain is NO_INFORMATION.2

A second, independent assessment was obtained from: gpt-5 Codex (openai family), via `codex exec`3

The assessment above was made by: Claude Opus 5 (anthropic family)4

How the second assessor was asked: Blind, from scripts/second_assessor_prompt.py, which assembles the prompt from an ALLOW-LIST of registry-sourced factual fields and refuses to send it if any RoB 2 verdict word appears in the assembled text. The second assessor was not shown this assessment and was not asked whether it agreed. It was given this project's NO_INFORMATION-never-LOW rule so the comparison measures judgement rather than house dialect.5

The disagreement rate, reported as disagreement because agreement between two assessors given the same facts authenticates nothing: 9 of 18 judgements -- 50.0%. Reported as disagreement: agreement between two assessors given the same facts authenticates nothing.6

Where they disagree, by domain: D1 3 of 3 disagree, D2 0 of 3 disagree, D3 0 of 3 disagree, D4 0 of 3 disagree, D5 3 of 3 disagree and overall 3 of 3 disagree.7

That rate was measured before this review's D1 judgements moved. It is left as measured: On 2026-08-21 this review's D1 judgements moved from LOW to NO_INFORMATION on the RoB 2 guidance -- the position assessor 2 had taken. The rate above was measured before that and is left exactly as measured: it is a published number, it is the record of what a blind second assessor said, and it is the reason the guidance was re-read. Editing it would delete the evidence that the change was warranted. This is the same computation re-run on the object as it now stands, so both are visible and neither is silently corrected.8

Re-run on the object as it now stands: 6 of 18 judgements -- 33.3%. By domain: D1 0 of 3 disagree, D2 0 of 3 disagree, D3 0 of 3 disagree, D4 0 of 3 disagree, D5 3 of 3 disagree and overall 3 of 3 disagree.9

Certainty of the evidence

Certainty was rated with GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons..1

No domain is rated UP. Rating up for a large effect or a dose-response gradient applies to observational evidence that has not already been rated down, and neither condition holds here.2

Certainty VERY_LOW. The risk-of-bias domain reads the per-result RoB 2 assessments made 2026-08-20 and named above, not a topic-level summary; indirectness reads the estimand findings recorded on this pool.3

Where a result is rated worse than LOW overall, the domain carrying that judgement is: D5 on 3 result(s). The overall rating is the worst domain, so these are the domains that determine it.4

D3 is NO_INFORMATION and the threat is larger than icosapent's for the same reason at a different scale: a fixed measurement at DAY 510 is roughly seventeen months of attrition risk against twelve weeks. (rating: serious); inconsistency: MODERATE to LOW, down 1 level(s) -- I-squared is 74.1% with tau-squared 10.6 over k=3. Handbook 10.10.2 warns against reading I-squared mechanically, and at this k the estimate is imprecise -- but the point estimates themselves differ materially and the direction of the finding does not rest on the statistic alone. (rating: serious); indirectness: LOW to VERY_LOW, down 1 level(s) -- the pooled co-primary is one of two and the selection is unrecorded. Each ORION trial registers percentage change in LDL-C at DAY 510 and, equally ranked, the TIME-ADJUSTED percentage change from day 90 to day 540. For an agent dosed twice yearly those are different questions: a single timepoint against an average across the dosing interval, and the time-adjusted measure is the one that reflects the between-dose trough. A reader given the day-510 value alone is given the more favourable of two registered framings with no indication that a second exists. (rating: serious); imprecision: not rated down -- k=3 with 482, 1561 and 1617 participants -- 3,660 in total -- and an interval of -58.3 to -49.64 that is narrow relative to the effect and far from the null. Optimal information size is met for a continuous lipid endpoint at this scale. Handbook 15.6.2. Not rated down, and this is the domain on which inclisiran differs from the other two. (rating: not serious); publication bias: not rated down -- not assessed rather than assessed as ABSENT. Funnel-plot asymmetry and its tests are uninformative below about ten studies -- Handbook 13.3.5.4 -- and these pools carry two or three. 'Undetected' here means nobody looked with an instrument that could see, not that publication bias is unlikely. Not rated down, because rating down on an unmeasurable domain would invent a defect. (rating: undetected)

Discussion

[Draft] The pooled MD is -53.97 (95% CI -58.3 to -49.64) over 3 trials. Certainty is rated VERY_LOW. Every contributing interval excludes no effect. Whether a change of that magnitude is clinically meaningful in this population is the author's judgement: no field on this object records a threshold of importance, and none is assumed here.1

[Draft] Across 3 trials, tau-squared 10.5954; every trial interval excludes no effect. Whether that degree of disagreement matters clinically -- whether the trials are answering the same question in the same patients -- is the author's judgement.2

[Draft] This review pools -53.97 (95% CI -58.3 to -49.64) over 3 trials. The appraised synthesis pooled an outcome not recorded here. Why the two results differ -- whether by population, outcome definition, model or included set -- is the author's judgement.3

[Draft] The evidence base is 3 trials, assessed for risk of bias as SOME_CONCERNS on 3 result(s). GRADE certainty is VERY_LOW. Whether that is enough to answer the question depends on the decision the answer is for, which is not stated on this object, and is the author's judgement.4

[Draft] Certainty was not rated down on any GRADE domain. What further evidence would change the conclusion is a judgement about a trial nobody has run, and is the author's.5

Refused: a sentence that would have been composed around an absence marker -- the field it needed records only that it was never recorded6

Comparison with published syntheses

Published syntheses were identified as follows. PubMed E-utilities; query, counts and a per-record decision in ssot/inclisiran-lipid-kidney-auto-full-review/appraisal/PUBLISHED_SYNTHESIS_SCREEN.json. 61 records matched, 30 retrieved, 10 appraised. The remaining 51 were not read and that is stated in the screen file rather than left to be inferred from the number.1

This review was compared against 4 published synthesis(es); the denominator is stated because a comparison against an unstated number of reviews is not a comparison.2

Where our result differs from theirs: Not by trial set, which is the unusual and useful thing about this comparison. The closest synthesis pools the same three trials and differs by about three percentage points, so the difference is in extraction or in which registered co-primary was taken -- day 510, or time-adjusted day 90 to 540. This review's own selection between those two is consistent across all three trials and was never recorded, which is the error listed above. The broader syntheses agree with this review closely; the real-world pooling does not, and its own authors attribute that to baseline LDL-C and adherence rather than to either estimate being wrong.3
